To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the formation of a sequence of ultrashort laser pulses in a Yttrium Aluminum Garnet (YAG) laser was found to depend on the intensity of the radiation in the active material relative to the intensity of radiation in a nonlinear absorbers.
we have found a way to improve the contrast of ultrashort laser pulses by using nonlinear absorbers.

the process of formation of a trainof ultrashort pulses is strongly dependent on the radiation intensities of the active material and a nonlinear absorber and the presence of two thresholds, one for the free-oscillations and the other for the formation of the ultrashort pulses, is an indication of the optimal selection of the conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high-power neodymum laser for plasma heating.
the investigation of the processes of formation of a train.of ultrashort pulses (USP) in a YAG laser.
the development of the theory and practice of the use of ultrashort laser pulses in plasma physics and in the investigation of high-temperature plasma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present investigation has provided means for improving the quality of the ultrashort pulses generated in a neodymium-garnet laser and for increasing their reproducibility from one flash to the next.
this work represents a major contribution to the understanding of the physics of laser oscillations, particularly in the area of nonlinear optics.
the present investigation provided means of improving considerably the quality of the output radiation of a YAG:Ni laser and of increasing its stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of ultrashhort pulses in the laser was due to the nonlinear interaction of the radiation with a nonlinear absorber, the radiation intensity in the absorber being determined by the radiation intensity in an active medium.
the formation of a stable train of ultrashhort pulses is a promising method of improving the contrast of radiation in solid state lasers.
the present work is a good starting point for further research in this field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the laser output is very sensitive to the intensity of the radiation in the nonlinear absorber.
we have demonstrated the ability to produce a train of ultrahigh contrast pulses from a single mode Nd:YAG laser.
the contrast of ultrashort-pulse generation can be increased considerably by the selection of optimal conditions of operation of a solid-state laser.
